Subaru Natsuki is suddenly transported from Japan to a fantasy world, where he has no money, special powers, or idea how to get by. After three deaths, he realizes he returns to an earlier point whenever he dies—a power he calls “Return by Death.” [3][4][19][20]

In repeated attempts to help the silver-haired girl who first rescued him, Subaru learns that she is pursuing a stolen badge. The thief, Felt, and her companion Rom are caught up in a deal with Elsa, a deadly assassin. Subaru initially fails to prevent the violence, but on his next attempt he chooses to intervene, despite his fear. [10][11][21][43][44]

When Elsa attacks the group in the loot cellar, Subaru helps Felt escape and fights alongside the girl and her spirit, Puck. Felt finds Reinhard, who arrives and drives Elsa off. Subaru protects the girl from Elsa’s final strike, but is badly wounded. Before losing consciousness, he asks the girl her name; she tells him she is Emilia and thanks him for saving her. [49][52][64][76][77][94][95][99][101]

Emilia treats Subaru, and decides to take him with her, both to learn more about him and because he saved her. [28][32]

Crusch led an expedition of roughly 220 soldiers, supported by the Iron Fangs, to ambush the White Whale at the Great Flugel Tree. Subaru’s metia signaled its arrival, and Rem’s opening ice attack broke the initial hesitation; the force followed with magic-crystal cannon fire, while Crusch and Wilhelm struck at close range. Night Repel lit the battlefield, and the attackers’ coordinated assault wounded the Whale, but it stayed aloft. [1][36][38][42][43][46][48]

Wilhelm and the Iron Fangs kept up the pressure, and Wilhelm eventually gouged out the Whale’s eye. The beast retaliated with its mist: it scattered the force, drove some to madness, and erased those it swallowed from everyone’s memories. Anti-magic crystals thinned the mist, but the Whale split into three, leaving the battered survivors facing a desperate fight. [49][50][73][75][80][84][90]

Subaru rallied the demoralized fighters and worked out that the three were one Whale divided into weaker bodies. He and Rem drew its attention; Rem’s ice spear helped lure the main body down, and the force felled the Great Flugel Tree onto it. Wilhelm then delivered the finishing blow, dedicating it to his wife, Theresia. [52][59][90][103][109][110]

After the costly battle in Pristella, Subaru’s group set out east to seek the Sage in the Auguria Dunes, hoping to find a way to restore what had been lost—names, memories, and bodies. The journey from Roswaal Manor to the dunes took twenty days. The dunes were notorious for demon beasts, miasma, and warped space that could leave travelers circling without getting closer to the tower. Anastasia reasoned that the shifting “sand time” opened a route through the distortion, and Ram’s clairvoyance helped guide the party through it. [12][21][51][5]

Beyond the sand, they found a flower-filled field that was actually a gathering of oiran bears. When the bears attacked, the group fought their way through, with Meili summoning sandworms to help. [3][65][66]

At the tower, Subaru was killed by a light from it and returned by death; the party then faced further danger before reaching the guardian, Shaula. She mistook Subaru for her long-awaited master, Flugel, and revealed that the tower’s original purpose was as the Great Pleiades Library. [26][28][61][6]

Once reunited inside, the group learned that the tower’s third floor, Taygeta, was an examination hall: passing its puzzle was required to access the archive. [53][54]

Wilhelm was born the third son of a declining noble family and devoted himself to swordsmanship, eventually leaving home at fourteen to join the royal army. His extraordinary skill made him feared as the “Sword Devil,” but he lived for battle and kept others at a distance. [1][2][4][5]

During leave in the capital, he met Theresia, a young woman tending a hidden flower garden. Their repeated conversations gradually changed him: he began to see that he had taken up the sword to protect others, not merely because it was all he had. He became more considerate of his comrades and accepted a knighthood. [10][12][16][17][18]

When he learned his family’s land was under attack, Wilhelm rushed home without orders. He fought desperately, but the enemy overwhelmed him. Wounded and facing death, he remembered the people in his life, especially Theresia, and realized how lonely his life had been. He did not want to die. [19][20]

Rem and her twin sister Ram were born into a demon tribe that considered twins abominations because each had only one horn. The chief nearly ordered them killed, but Ram’s extraordinary magical power saved them. [3]

Ram’s talent made her the tribe’s pride, while Rem—whose abilities were ordinary—admired her and struggled to measure up. Even her family’s love and her people’s encouragement felt painful beside the constant comparison. [1][2]

During a fire that destroyed their village, Rem found her parents among the dead and encountered black-robed attackers. Ram arrived to protect her, but Rem’s envy surfaced when Ram’s horn was broken. Rem later felt deep shame and guilt for that thought, especially as Ram lost her former strength and Rem came to help care for her. [11][13][5]
